Let me tell you a story of a search engine who wanted to be the best search engine it could be.

Like any search engine it wants to give you the results that match yoru search, and because it wants to be a good search engine, it wants to sort them by how relevant they are to you.

But how does this search engine know what you mean by the words you give it? How does it evaluate relevance?

Should it just give you all the files the name of which matches your query?

Should it sort documents by how often they contain the terms of your query?

It wanted to be the best search engine it could be, so it first looked at all the web pages on the internet it could find, and then grouped them by how tightly they linked to each other. And it discovered that a single word can have many meanings in different contexts. And that words can be spelled and misspelt in many ways. And that words can have synonyms, depending on context.

So whenever some hapless user would give it a query to process, it would first work out which group it most likely fell into, and rank the results within that group. This way it could return results that were relevant even if the documents did not contain the exact same words as the query, but synonyms and alternate spellings as well.

And sometimes, things that were relevant in one particular sub-group were helpful in other sub-groups of the same group as well.

So if someone wanted to know how to fix an issue with one particular brand of internal combustion engine, the best description could often be found taking another brand's motor as an example. And if a common network chip needed closed-source drivers to work with an operating system kernel, and the developer had put up a robots.txt file preventing the search engine from refering to it directly, the links and descriptions could often be found in popular forums of one distribution or another.

It tried to be as helpful as possible, and not be hampered by those who tried to game the way it worked.

But no matter how hard it tried, and how smart it became, it could only ever retrieve the information that others had helpfully provided.
